sentences.text: Fadenia was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the order Eugeneodontiformes, a group defined by the presence of tooth whorls.
Individuals of this genus could grow to approximately 1.5 meters in length, and two species are recognized within the genus: Fadenia crenulata and Fadenia gigas.
Fadenia was one of the few eugeneodont genera to survive the end-Permian mass extinction and represents one of the latest survivors of the group.
The genus was first described in 1932 by Danish paleontologist Eigil Nielsen, who discovered the fossils while participating in the Three-year Expedition to East Greenland led by Lauge Koch.
The genus name Fadenia honors Gunnar Seidenfaden, the manager of the expedition.
Fadenia is classified within the family Caseodontidae, and a later classification authority for the genus is P. Aellen and C. C. Townsend, 1972.
Fadenia fossils have been found in the Carboniferous of Missouri, the Permian of Greenland, and the Early Triassic of British Columbia.
